title: Jasmine Tea Custard Ice Cream with Sugared Cherries
changes_from_base: Jasmine green tea steeped in the dairy instead of vanilla, with syrup-plumped dried cherries layered through.
summary: Our classic custard infused with jasmine green tea instead of vanilla and layered with dried cherries plumped in sugar syrup. Fragrant, delicate and fruity.

ingredients.note: syrup drained; nutrition counts about half

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Plump the cherries
steps.text: Boil the water and sugar in the small saucepan until the sugar dissolves, pour over the cherries in a heatproof bowl and leave to cool, then refrigerate.

steps.title: Steep the tea
steps.text: Bring the cream, milk and sugar just to the boil, remove from the heat, add the tea leaves and steep for 6 min. Strain, pressing on the leaves, and return to the pan; green tea turns bitter if steeped longer.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Beat the yolks, whisk in two ladles of the tea dairy and pour back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir gently over low heat until the custard reaches 77-80 °C and lightly coats the spatula.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Add the salt, strain and cool over the iced water, then refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and layer
steps.text: Churn until thick. Drain the cherries well and layer them with the ice cream in the container.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Press baking paper onto the surface, cover and freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Use loose jasmine green tea rather than bags for a cleaner, stronger flavour.
A common mistake is adding wet cherries, which freeze into icy lumps. Drain them thoroughly.
Plumped cherries keep for a month in the fridge.
storage: Freeze in a covered container for up to 2 weeks.
